title: The Global-State Trap
description: An evaluator that keeps a global symbol table. Shared mutable state is the single most common reason test suites fail intermittently.

steps.description: This is the bad pattern: an evaluator that keeps a global symbol table. The page says shared mutable state is the single most common reason test suites fail intermittently.
The comment labels it BAD because global state leaks between tests. `_global_env = {}` is one dictionary shared by every call.
`evaluate` uses `_global_env` directly, so a binding written in one call survives into the next.

steps.question: The page says if test A binds x = 5 and test B asks for x, test B may pass even though it should raise what?
